match.reason: No bank point covers the full range of sources in this point: the closest, bus-financing-new-business, covers only owner's savings and bank debt, and leaves out leasing, investors and crowdfunding and the cost, control and size factors, so it is narrower and adapting it would need a new idea rather than small changes.

draft.title: Sources of finance
card: Owner's savings
money the owner puts in from their own pocket. It costs no interest and gives away no control, but the amount is often small.
Loan
money borrowed from a bank or lender and paid back with interest. The owner keeps full ownership but must make repayments.
Investors
people who put in money in return for a share of the business. The business gets more funds, but the owner shares control and profits.
Leasing and crowdfunding
leasing means paying regular fees to use equipment instead of buying it. Crowdfunding means raising small amounts from many people, often online.
draft.remember: Choose finance by weighing its cost, the control given up and what the business needs.

a.q: Priya starts a bakery in Ballarat. She sells a 30% share of it to a friend who puts in money. Which source of finance is this?
a.why: The friend gives money in return for a share of the business, so this is investor finance. It is not a loan, because a loan is paid back with interest and does not give the lender a share of the business.
a.clue: The friend now owns part of the business.

b.q: Tom opens a bike repair shop in Geelong. He wants to keep full ownership and sole control, and he can afford regular repayments. Which source of finance suits him best?
opts: Handing over part of the profits to a partner
Raising money from a share offer to the public
b.why: A loan lets Tom keep full ownership and control, as long as he makes repayments with interest. Investors would own a share of the business, so they would have a say and a part of the profits.
b.clue: Which source lets the lender be repaid without owning any of the business?

problems.detail: The clue mentions 'the lender' being 'repaid', which practically names the loan option. A student can pick 'A bank loan' from the clue's wording without weighing ownership and control.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one clearly right answer. The only issue is that question b's clue uses the words 'lender' and 'repaid', which gives the answer away.

a.q: Priya starts a bakery in Ballarat. She sells a 30% share of it to a friend who puts in money. Which source of finance is this?
a.why: The friend gives money in return for a share of the business, so this is investor finance. It is not a loan, because a loan is paid back with interest and does not give the lender a share of the business.

b.q: Tom opens a bike repair shop in Geelong. His savings will not cover the cash he needs to fit out the shop. He wants to keep full ownership and sole control, and he can afford regular repayments. Which source suits him best?
opts: A bank loan repaid with interest
Selling a 20% share to an investor
Bringing in investors who share profits
Selling shares in the shop to the public
b.why: A loan gives Tom the cash he needs while he keeps full ownership and control, as long as he makes repayments with interest. Every other option gives away a share of the business, so others would have a say and take part of the profits.
b.clue: Which option leaves every part of the shop in Tom's hands?

b.best: A bank loan repaid with interest
